To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
water stress during the grain-filling period induced senescence and promoted remobilization of C reserves from the peduncular tissues to the grains.

water stress at anthesis or post-anthesis stages promoted senescence and enhanced remobilization of stored food from vegetative tissues to grains in wheat, and the effect of water deficit on remobilization was more pronounced at the post-anthesis stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of drought stress at the post-anthesis stage on the remobilization of carbon reserves and some physiological changes in the flag leaf of two wheat cultivars differing in drought resistance.
the effect of drought at the post-anthesis stage on senescence and C remobilisation in two wheat cultivars.
the role of the flag leaf senescence and its relationship to remobilization of C reserves during grain filling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the senescing leaves and stems are the major source of C for grain filling in wheat, and water deficit during grain filling accelerates the senescence of the vegetative organs and promotes the remobilization and reallocation of the stored C to the developing grains.
the senescing process is not only the result of the remobilization of stored food, but also a prerequisite of the process.
water stress, at both WS1 and WS 2 stages, promoted the remobilization of C reserves from the stem to the grains, but this process was less efficient under WS2 than under WS1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water deficits during grain-filling promoted remobilization of C from vegetative tissues to grains by inducing the senescence of the flag leaf.

remobilization and re-allocation of C reserves in wheat plants are closely associated with the extent of leaf senescence induced under water deficits and the efficiency of this process is genotype-dependent.

water deficits, especially at the later stages, promote senescence and enhance remobilization of stored C from vegetative parts to the grain, but this process is more effective in drought-tolerant than in drought-sensitive genotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the remobilization of C reserves in wheat is a complex process and is influenced by many factors.
water deficits during grain-filling period promote the senescence of the flag leaves by accelerating the reduction in chlorophyll content and loss of proteins.

remobilization and transfer to grains is a complex process that involves a number of factors, including the rate of photosynthesis and its decline during senescence, and the rate of remobilization of pre-stored carbon reserves in vegetative organs to the grains.
